title: Connect active-Agent self-review to the alignment Adapter

requirement.summary: Implement the first host-neutral semantic-review execution slice by allowing the existing Alignment Adapter to pass only resolved normalized context to the active Coding Agent materializer, bind its observations to the exact medium-risk self-review route and Provider, and return an accepted advisory result without new user configuration.

objective.rationale: The Provider and risk-routing contracts are executable only after one host Adapter can materialize a normalized active-Agent self-review result through the existing user-facing alignment journey.

goal: Add a host-neutral active-Agent self-review materializer boundary, connect it to a resolved Alignment Adapter journey, enforce minimal normalized context and allowed evidence, and accept only the exact digest-bound advisory result with cross-host tests.
non_goals: Do not add a vendor SDK, model endpoint, model selection, API key, account configuration, network call, hosted service, background process, or independent Reviewer integration.
Do not put Codex, Claude Code, IDE, or model-specific enums, branches, prompts, credentials, or behavior into Core.
Do not send raw request text, raw answers, transcripts, assistant responses, full source content, model prompts, credentials, secrets, or absolute host paths into Core or retained journey state.
Do not run self-review before the human-owned alignment dialogue is resolved, use it for low risk, describe it as independent, or silently upgrade its assurance.

Do not let the materializer invent evidence outside the allowed repository references, select a direction, modify requirements or ADRs, admit tasks, start sessions, or authorize code, scope, exceptions, Git, publication, release, deployment, production, or external writes.
Do not change stable 0.2.1, immutable v0.3.0rc1, release metadata, workflows, consumer repositories, or external systems.
acceptance_signals: A host-neutral ActiveAgentSelfReviewMaterializer protocol receives only an ephemeral normalized context derived from the exact resolved AlignmentStreamResponse, self-review route, active-host Provider, and explicitly allowed repository evidence references.

ReferenceAlignmentAdapter exposes one end-to-end self-review operation only after the human-owned dialogue is resolved; existing natural-language request, clarification, and single-select behavior remains unchanged.

The operation deterministically selects the medium-risk active-Agent self-review route, invokes the supplied host materializer exactly once, builds and accepts the exact Provider/route-digest-bound advisory result, and returns privacy/authority disclosures without retaining raw conversation.

The Adapter generates observation identities and rejects unknown draft fields, empty or oversized output, duplicate observations, evidence outside the allowed set, sensitive or host-local content, false authority, stale Provider/route/result bindings, and assurance substitution.

Low-risk no-review, unresolved dialogue, ready-but-unselected dialogue, unavailable or non-active Provider, independent-review Provider, unsupported risk, materializer failure, and malformed materializer output fail before an accepted result exists.
Codex and Claude Code active-host fixtures both execute through the same Adapter/materializer contract, while Core source contains no vendor-specific enum or special case.

No implementation code performs network I/O, loads credentials, starts an Agent, selects a model, writes repository/runtime state, or applies a human choice; the current Coding Agent host remains responsible for actually supplying semantic inference.

Affected source-of-truth and public documentation accurately distinguishes the implemented host execution seam and offline cross-host rehearsal from a production model SDK or independent Reviewer integration.
Focused/full tests, current-task, scope, repository, schemas, compile, and diff validation pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_active_agent_self_review tests.test_reference_alignment_adapter tests.test_semantic_review tests.test_alignment_transport tests.test_clarification_dialogue tests.test_agent_skills tests.test_task_contract tests.test_user_documentation tests.test_portfolio_docs -v

items: Calling the same Agent after it developed a solution may create confirmation bias even when the result is accurately labeled self-review.
Passing too much alignment or source context could leak raw conversation, local paths, credentials, or undeclared repository content.
A permissive materializer could invent evidence, overstate independence, or make its advisory observation look like a human decision.
An Adapter-only callback can be mistaken for a finished production host integration unless the offline evidence and open SDK/UI boundary remain explicit.

stop_conditions: Stop if the self-review can run before the final human alignment selection or can alter that selection.
Stop if the materializer receives or persists raw conversation, credentials, secrets, model prompts, full undeclared source content, or absolute host paths.
Stop if the active Agent can be labeled independent or if an unavailable/non-active Provider can produce an accepted result.
Stop if observations can cite evidence outside the explicit allowed repository references or grant any project/external authority.
Stop if ordinary use requires a second model, new account, vendor SDK, API key, or network service.
Stop before any external model call, Provider setup, network access, external write, Git write, publication, release, deployment, or consumer mutation.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the completed active-Agent materializer seam and explicitly requested the next live foreground transport feature on 2026-08-06.
